blocks.text: Seth’s hands closed around the crooked turret.
blocks.alt: Dork reaches toward the firing control while Zerdo grips the crooked turret’s damaged lower rim.

blocks.text: Inside the hull, Dork reached for a steering lever.
One track ground forward. The other held, dragging the locked turret back toward Terminal Tower.
The damaged mounting creaked under Seth’s palms.
Seth dug in his boots.
The tank kept turning. His heels skidded a foot across the pavement.
“Jenny!”
“Going!”
She was already running for the hull.
“Say goodbye to your tower!” Dork shouted.
Seth wrenched sideways with everything he had.
The barrel jerked off its line. Dork fired.
Blue light tore across the square. It missed the tower, raked along the empty curb and struck a streetlamp’s bolted light fitting.
The lamp head shrank to the size of a coffee cup, slipped free of its mount and dropped into the gutter with a clang.
blocks.alt: Zerdo forces the crooked mounted ray away from Terminal Tower as one blue shot shrinks a single streetlamp head at the empty curb.

blocks.text: “Heads down!” Billy yelled.
Seth forced the barrel down toward the empty curb.
The beam winked out.
Seth hauled the barrel skyward. His shoulders burned.
For an instant, he almost called for Flaming Head.
Flaming Head wasn’t here.
Dork’s right hand left the firing switch.
He grabbed the reverse lever.
Seth saw the opening.
Only a second.
Enough.
Above the rooftops, Fist banked around a chimney. Jaws stayed on his tail.
“You really don’t know me,” Fist said.
Jaws snapped at the air beside him. “Should I?”
The teeth clanged shut an inch from the cuff.
blocks.alt: Fist rolls away as Jaws snaps his metal teeth just behind the repaired red cuff with an inset white panel.

blocks.text: Fist slid away.
“No.”
It came out quieter than he meant.
Jaws didn’t notice. His eyes had slid past him, down to the street.
To the police car. To the woman beside the open door.
“Laura!” Jaws called. “You want out?”
Laura looked up.
She smiled.
“About time.”
Below, Dork slammed the reverse lever.
The tracks roared. The tank lurched backward, and Jenny, halfway up the hull, went off it like a cork.
She hit the pavement, rolled and came up with both white gloves scraped gray.
blocks.alt: Jenny rolls clear of the reversing tank while orange-suited Zerdo braces beside it and grips the still-attached crooked turret.

blocks.text: “I’m fine!” she called, before anyone could ask.
The tank kept pulling away. Seth kept his grip on the turret.
The tracks tore at the street. Chunks of asphalt flew. The engine screamed.
Seth stayed where he was.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
Bolts cracked around the turret ring.
Steel shrieked.
The whole top of the tank came up in his hands.
blocks.alt: Zerdo tears the complete turret clear of the tank, with its copper emitter attached and its firing cable disconnected.

blocks.text: A black cable stretched beneath it. It pulled out of its socket and dangled loose.
Dork jabbed the firing control. The copper opening stayed dark.
He looked up through the empty ring.
“Your gun’s come loose,” Seth said.
Dork snatched at the torn lead.
“Jenny!”
“I see it!”
Jenny reached the driver’s opening.
Her white glove closed around Dork’s wrist.
“Out.”
He snatched his other hand toward the controls. She caught that one too.
“Do you know what that cost?” Dork snarled.
“You stole it.”
She hauled him through the hatch and onto the street. His shoes scraped the armor all the way down.
blocks.alt: Jenny pulls Dork from the lower hull driver opening while Zerdo holds the detached turret safely aside.

blocks.text: Billy waved two officers around the planter.
“This way. Keep him behind cover.”
An officer fastened cuffs behind Dork’s back. The other took his arm.
blocks.alt: Billy directs two officers as they take the struggling Dork into custody behind a stone planter.

blocks.text: Billy opened his notebook. “Mr. Orkleson? Just one question, and then I’ll leave you with the officers. You said you’d take the tower home. Where, exactly? I only ask because I can’t see how it fits.”
“I had a spot picked out!”
“Of course you did.” Billy wrote that down.
Seth lowered the turret to the pavement, copper opening pointed at the sky.
Jenny knelt beside it. “Tool rack,” Seth said. She fetched a wrench from beside the driver’s seat, loosened the retaining nuts and drew the ray out of its cradle in one pull.
blocks.alt: Jenny releases the ray’s mounting inside the detached turret while Zerdo steadies it on the street.

blocks.text: She carried the ray to Billy.
“Don’t touch the controls.”
Billy carried it away, an officer at his elbow.
Above the square, Jaws dived.
He dropped like a stone toward the police car, teeth wide, aimed at the door hinges.
blocks.alt: Jaws dives toward Laura’s police cruiser with Fist pursuing from above.

blocks.text: “Laura! Duck!”
Laura didn’t duck.
She leaned out past the officer’s arm and spat.
A bright glob of plasma hit the stack of wooden boards beside the planter. They burst into flame.
The officer with the extinguisher dived toward the fire.
His partner pulled Laura back from the door. She was still smiling.
Fist cut across the dive.
His knuckles struck the side of the iron jaw.
blocks.alt: Fist punches Jaws away from Laura’s cruiser while cuffed Laura fires plasma at wooden boards and an officer approaches with an extinguisher.

blocks.text: Jaws flew sideways, away from the car, and slammed into the cleared square. He rolled, whirled and came back up.
Fist hung in the air between him and the police.
“You’ll have to get past me.”
Jaws stared at him.
“Gladly.”
Seth stood over the dead turret.
Beside him, the tank sat headless, its engine ticking.
“That’s all of it?” Jenny said.
Seth looked at the open ring. No copper. No machine. Only steel.
“That’s all of it.”
She checked the empty driver’s compartment. A towing chain hung in clips along the hull. She unhooked it and laid it on the curb.
Then she checked the street.
Dork and his guards were clear. Billy and the ray were clear. The officers had Laura behind her door.
blocks.alt: Billy carries the disconnected ray behind cover as Jenny checks the empty hull and signals Zerdo.

blocks.text: She stepped back.
“All yours.”
Seth took the empty turret shell and lifted it overhead.
blocks.alt: Zerdo raises the empty turret shell overhead, with its front emitter opening visibly empty.

blocks.text: Behind the planter, Dork stopped struggling.
“No! That’s an Army tank!”
Seth looked at the hull.
“I know.”
He brought the shell down.
blocks.alt: Zerdo smashes the empty turret shell across the vacant hull, folding armor and buckling the tracks.

blocks.text: The crash rolled between the buildings. The hull folded beneath the blow. One track snapped loose and spilled across the pavement. The other buckled under the weight.
Dust burst around Seth’s boots.
He let the turret settle into the crushed armor and stepped back.
The engine coughed once.
Then it stopped.
The dust hung over the wreck like fog.
Jaws turned at the crash.
He saw Dork behind the planter. He saw the folded steel. He saw the empty ring where the turret had been.
His eyes went back to the glove.
“That’s it,” he said. “I’m done playing.”
He came in fast, teeth open.
blocks.alt: Jaws charges Fist above the wrecked tank while the glove waits and begins a last-second dodge.

blocks.text: Fist waited.
Closer.
The white panel on his red cuff twitched.
Jaws stopped dead.
He had been about to bite. Instead he hung there, a foot from the glove, eyes narrowed.
“No,” he said. “I don’t think I will.”
Fist didn’t move.
He’s learning.
He let the cuff drift lower. Close to the crushed hull. Close to a torn edge of steel.
Jaws’s mean streak did the rest.
He lunged.
Fist dropped away.
The iron teeth slammed into the folded armor and screeched along it. Jaws jerked back with a howl, his jaw buzzing.
blocks.alt: Fist slips beneath the bite as Jaws’s iron teeth strike torn tank armor; his red cuff has an inset white panel and the wreck’s emitter hole is empty.

blocks.text: Fist came up beneath him and drove upward with everything in the glove.
His knuckles caught the iron jaw.
Jaws flew out of the dust and hit clear pavement. He skidded to a stop beside the wreck.
blocks.alt: Jaws lies dazed on clear pavement beside the wreck while Fist guards him and Jenny approaches.

blocks.text: For a moment his eyes would not focus.
Fist hovered above him, cuff safely out of reach.
Jenny arrived with the towing chain.
“Keep him there.”
Before Jaws could open his teeth, she passed the chain around the closed metal jaw. Seth came beside her and pulled it snug against the iron plates, leaving Jaws’s nose and eyes clear.
They fastened the short tether to the tank’s undamaged rear towing eye.
Jaws tried to rise. The chain drew tight.
He tried his teeth. The links held the halves together.
Seth kept a hand on the chain. Fist did not move away.
An officer called for equipment to move him under guard.
The last boards burned out behind the planter. The officer with the extinguisher put his foot on the final ember.
Across the street, Laura watched Jenny walk back to her escort.
“Still want me on your team?”
Jenny looked at the scorched boards. Then at her.
“If you want to help.”
Laura looked away. She gave no answer.

Billy stepped out from behind the planter, the ray safe beside an officer. He crouched and picked the toy-sized lamp head out of the gutter. He turned it over in his fingers. “Nobody ever remembers the lamp,” he said, and wrote it down. Then he slipped it into his coat pocket.
Dork sat between his guards and glared at the tank.
Fist watched Jaws. Seth held the tether.
blocks.alt: Orange-suited Zerdo holds the anchored jaw tether beside the wreck while older Billy keeps the miniature lamp in his coat pocket, the captured ray rests under guard, and Laura stands cuffed behind her back.

blocks.text: Above them, every window of Terminal Tower caught the sun.
Seth looked up.
Still there.
